Commentary.Commentary: In all readiness for Bangladesh's reply to get underway. The umpires are out in the field and so are the players of Netherlands. Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan will be the opening pair for Bangladesh. Aryan Dutt will get the new ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Bangladesh will be confident enough to chase this total on a surface that, despite its unpredictability, has played fairly well. Slower balls proved effective and were tougher to put away. For Netherlands, early wickets in the Powerplay will be crucial if they are to stand any chance. Back in a bit for the chase.

Saif Hassan is up for a quick chat. He thanks the almighty for the opportunity and feels elated to deliver for the team. He shares that he had a conversation with the captain about the plans, and he tried bowling in the right areas and eventually got the wickets in the process.

Teja Nidamanuru was slow to get going before stitching together a partnership with captain Scott Edwards. For a brief while, it looked promising with the two experienced men at the crease, but both fell in the same over and that proved decisive. From there, the Bangladesh bowlers tightened the screws by chipping away at wickets. That said, late efforts from Aryan Dutt and Tim Pringle have added some respectability to the total. Taskin Ahmed was the star with the ball for Bangladesh with figures of 4 for 28 from his 4 overs.

32 runs off the last 3 overs have given Netherlands something to bowl at but 136 does not seem enough at the halfway mark. An innings that never really took off for the Dutch. Apart from the first three overs, where Max O’Dowd came out attacking, Bangladesh controlled proceedings really well. Max provided a brisk start but couldn’t carry on, while his partner Vikramjit Singh endured a real struggle at the other end.

Commentary.Commentary: Mustafizur Rahman starts from over the wicket. Keeps it on a length, pushed across the right-hander, outside off. Teja Nidamanuru tentatively pokes at it and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Mustafizur Rahman to Teja Nidamanuru, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: An effort ball from Shoriful Islam as he bangs in a bumper, over middle, Vikramjit Singh ducks under it. A much better over from Shoriful.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Shoriful Islam to Vikramjit Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and wide on off, there to be put away, Vikramjit Singh sets up to slap it away but the ball holds in the surface and it is miscued off the inner half to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Shoriful Islam to Vikramjit Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that could have gone anywhere! Shoriful Islam bends his back and goes short, around the left shoulder. Vikramjit Singh is caught in a tangle and takes his eyes off the ball. Tries to fend it down but the ball catches the gloves and lobs but drops beside him safely.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Shoriful Islam to Vikramjit Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a hard length, on middle, Vikramjit Singh hops and lifts his front leg to help it away fine on the leg side but fails to lay any bat on it. The ball hits him on the thigh pad and drops in front.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Shoriful Islam to Vikramjit Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! On middle and leg, on a good length, Teja Nidamanuru steps out and swings to go big on the leg side. Gets beaten on the inside edge and a leg bye is taken as the ball drops off the pads in front of square leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Shoriful Islam to Teja Nidamanuru, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Change of ends for Shoriful Islam! Full and going across the right-hander, Teja Nidamanuru goes for the drive away from his body. Miscues it off an inside edge towards mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Shoriful Islam to Teja Nidamanuru, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Off-pace delivery, on a back of a length,on off, Teja jabs it off the back foot in front of mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Taskin Ahmed to Teja Nidamanuru, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Keeps the stumps in play, on a good length, Teja Nidamanuru dabs it down on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Taskin Ahmed to Teja Nidamanuru, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This nips back a bit, on a good length, on the off stump, Teja Nidamanuru firms the drive to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Taskin Ahmed to Teja Nidamanuru, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Honing in at the stumps, full in length, Teja Nidamanuru is caught in his crease but manages to bring his bat out in front to keep it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Taskin Ahmed to Teja Nidamanuru, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! In the channel on off, on a length, a hint of away shape, Teja defends slightly away from his body and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Taskin Ahmed to Teja Nidamanuru, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Teja Nidamanuru is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Taskin Ahmed strikes with his first ball! Max O'Dowd's breezy start has been cut short. Taskin steams in from over the wicket and lands it on a good length, attacking the stumps. Max closes the bat face and looks to flick it away. Closes the bat face early and gets a leading edge. The ball gets ballooned towards cover where Jaker Ali takes a dolly. Taskin lets out a roar and he is all pumped up.
Commentary.Howout: c Jaker Ali b Taskin Ahmed
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Taskin Ahmed to Max O'Dowd, OUT! c Jaker Ali b Taskin Ahmed.

Commentary.Commentary: Change! Taskin Ahmed joins the attack, replacing Shoriful Islam.
Quicker and flatter, at the stumps, on a nagging length, Max nudges it to long on for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Mahedi Hasan to Max O'Dowd, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower through the air and this grips a bit in the surface, on a length, around leg, Max O'Dowd gets forward to smother the spin but ekes out an inside edge onto the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Mahedi Hasan to Max O'Dowd, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Clean strike! Mahedi errs in length and serves it right in the slot, on the off stump. Max O'Dowd puts his front foot down the line of the ball and swings through. Tonks it to the left of long on for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Mahedi Hasan to Max O'Dowd, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on the pads, clipped through mid-wicket for a single by Singh.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Mahedi Hasan to Vikramjit Singh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slanting into the left-hander, tucking the batter up room, on the fuller side, Vikramjit Singh presses forwad to block and gets an inide edge onto the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Mahedi Hasan to Vikramjit Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flat and short, on off, Max O'Dowd rocks back and taps it to long on for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Mahedi Hasan to Max O'Dowd, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On the shorter side, on off, Max punches it to deep cover and takes the single. An expensive first over from Shoriful Islam. 13 runs off it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Shoriful Islam to Max O'Dowd, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Around off, on a length, Max O'Dowd caresses the drive down the deck. It is hit too straight and the ball hits the stumps at the bowling end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Shoriful Islam to Max O'Dowd, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Max O'Dowd takes the aerial route this time! On a length, outside off, Max O'Dowd lets his hands flow into the shot and carves it over wide mid off for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Shoriful Islam to Max O'Dowd, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Easy pickings! Full and this swings onto the pads from Islam, Max just tickles it fine to beat the diving short fine leg fielder to his right for four more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Shoriful Islam to Max O'Dowd, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: This moves away off the deck, on a good length, Max O'Dowd brings his bat out in front to block it out but ends up defending inside the line and the ball zips past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Shoriful Islam to Max O'Dowd, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Lovely shot! On a back of a length, going across, Max O'Dowd stands tall and punches it between cover and point for the first boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Shoriful Islam to Max O'Dowd, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: It will be pace in the form of Shoriful Islam from the other end.
A half-tracker, on off, Max O'Dowd gets on the back foot and thumps it to the left of long on. Wants to come back for the second but the long on fielder keeps the batters down to a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Mahedi Hasan to Max O'Dowd, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, fuller and on off, Vikramjit Singh presses forward and eases the drive to long off to open his account with one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Mahedi Hasan to Vikramjit Singh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: From over the wicket to the left-hander, sliding on with the arm from wide of the crease, on a nagging length, on middle, Singh backs away and hits it straight to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Mahedi Hasan to Vikramjit Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Max O'Dowd and Netherlands are underway! This is slower through the air, shorter and on off, O'Dowd turns it through the vacant mid-wicket region and gets off the mark with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Mahedi Hasan to Max O'Dowd, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another one from Mahedi that is fired in, on a length, around off, Max presses forward and knocks it to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Mahedi Hasan to Max O'Dowd, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pushed through from over the wicket, on a nagging length, at the stumps, Max O'Dowd goes right back and nudges it to square leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Mahedi Hasan to Max O'Dowd, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get going. Litton Das leads his men out to the middle. It will be Max O'Dowd and Vikramjit Singh to open the innings for Netherlands. Surprisingly, Bangladesh are starting with spin in the form of Mahedi Hasan. Hasan to Max with a slip in place. Let's play...

Before we get underway, the two teams will line up for the national anthems. The skies look clear for now, and let's hope it stays this way. It will be the Dutch national anthem first, followed by that of Bangladesh.

PITCH REPORT – Farveez Maharoof is near the deck. Mentions that there has been plenty of rain in the lead-up to the game, and the ground staff have worked tirelessly to get things ready. Tells that this wicket looks a bit different from usual, with some moisture still visible on the surface because of the rain. Adds that certain patches clearly show signs of dampness, which suggests there will be some assistance for Bangladesh’s bowlers early on. Informs that 10 of the last 13 games played here have been won by the teams chasing. States that the square boundaries measure 64 metres and 68 metres, while the straight hit is around 80 metres.

Scott Edwards, the skipper of Netherlands says that he is happy to bat first but would have chosen to bowl first as it's their first time playing on this pitch, which is a little bit different from their home conditions. Also says that it's a good opportunity for them to prepare for the World Cup. Ends by saying that they are going with three spinners and three seamers.

Litton Das, the skipper of Bangladesh says that it looks like a fresh pitch and they don't know how it will behave going forward. Mentions that they want to take advantage of the dew factor while chasing the total. He also points out that Sylhet has been a batter-friendly wicket, but there seems to be some grass left on the surface this time. Citing their recent good performance against Sri Lanka and Pakistan, he would like to carry forward their momentum in this series as well.
Netherlands (Playing XI) - Max O'Dowd, Vikramjit Singh, Teja Nidamanuru, Scott Edwards (C/WK), Shariz Ahmad, Noah Croes, Kyle Klein, Tim Pringle, Aryan Dutt, Paul van Meekeren, Daniel Doram.
Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon, Litton Das (C/WK), Saif Hassan, Tawhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali, Mahedi Hasan, Rishad Hossain, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam.
TOSS - Bangladesh win the toss and they will BOWL first.

For the Netherlands, this series presents a good opportunity to gain experience in subcontinental conditions ahead of the T20 World Cup next year. The last time they faced the Bangla Tigers and emerged victorious was in July 2012, and Scott Edwards and his squad will be eager to relive that glory and confront their rivals with unyielding pride. This series is not only crucial for national pride but also a chance for promising young players like Aryan Dutt, Cedric de Lange, Tim Pringle, and Shariz Ahmad to gain priceless experience and refine their skills against a side dominant at home. It rained in Sylhet yesterday, disrupting the training plans of both teams, and rain is forecasted during the match hours. Hopefully, the weather stays clear. Stay tuned for the toss and team updates coming your way shortly!

Looking back, the last showdown between these teams was at the T20 World Cup 2024, where Bangladesh triumphed by 25 runs. Since then, the hosts have had significant changes that have reshaped the squad, introducing fresh talent and new leadership. Under the astute guidance of Litton Das, the Bangla Tigers are riding high after consecutive series victories against formidable teams like Sri Lanka and Pakistan. One of the big calls ahead of the Asia Cup has been the omission of Mehidy Hasan Miraz, and with him not featuring in this series either, it opens the door for others to stake their claim in the XI.

Greetings to all the passionate cricket fans tuning in from across the globe! The atmosphere promises to be electric at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium as we gear up for the first encounter of the three-match T20I series between Bangladesh and the Netherlands. It is a historic occasion as the Dutch embark on their inaugural series in Bangladesh. For the Bangla Tigers, this is an invaluable chance to harness momentum as they prepare for the upcoming Asia Cup.
... MATCH DAY ...

We are in the midst of a bumper season of white-ball cricket, with The Hundred and the Caribbean Premier League driving the franchise action alongside a packed international calendar. Adding to the mix is the Netherlands’ tour of Bangladesh for a three-match T20I series, the first time the Dutch will play a bilateral series on Bangladeshi soil. All three matches will be played at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium. For Litton Das and his team, this series is an important chance to fine-tune their combinations ahead of the Asia Cup next month. Bangladesh’s T20I campaign in 2025 has been a mixed one, starting with setbacks against the UAE and Pakistan before bouncing back strongly with impressive wins over Sri Lanka and Pakistan. One of the main talking points is the return of wicketkeeper batter Nurul Hasan, who is back in the T20I side after almost three years. At the top of the order, Tanzid Hasan will open with a new partner after Mohammad Naim was dropped following a string of low scores. This puts added responsibility on Litton Das, who will be eager to regain form after a disappointing series against Pakistan. Tawhid Hridoy and Jaker Ali will be crucial in the middle order, while the all-rounder depth of Mohammad Saifuddin, Rishad Hossain, Mahedi Hasan and the returning Saif Hassan provides plenty of balance. In the pace department, Mustafizur Rahman’s variations remain the spearhead, with Taskin Ahmed, Shoriful Islam and Tanzim Hasan Sakib forming a solid support cast. On the other hand, the Netherlands come into this series aiming to build on the strides they have made in white-ball cricket over the past few years. Their upset wins at ICC events have underlined their potential, and with qualification for next year’s World Cup in India and Sri Lanka already secured in July, this tour offers a valuable chance to gain experience in Asian conditions. Scott Edwards’ leadership has been central to their growth, and alongside him, the likes of Max O'Dowd, Vikramjit Singh and Teja Nidamanuru will be key in providing batting stability. Whether he gets a game or not, it will be some experience for the 17-year-old batter, Cedric de Lange, who has impressed in the domestic circuit. In the all-rounder department, Tim Pringle and Sikander Zulfiqar provide balance, while Paul van Meekeren, Kyle Klein, and Sebastiaan Braat make up the pace attack. Aryan Dutt will lead the spin unit, supported by Daniel Doram, Shariz Ahmad, and Pringle. This is only the second bilateral series between Bangladesh and the Netherlands. The first came in 2021 in the Hague, when the spoils were shared in a two-match T20I series. Since then, the two sides have crossed paths three times at T20 World Cups, with Bangladesh winning on each occasion. Can the Dutch turn the tide this time, or will Bangladesh extend their dominance? We shall find out.
